HEXAGRAM NAME AND PRONUNCIATION:

[Traditional Chinese]

  渙（ㄏㄨㄢˋ）

[Simplified Chinese]

  涣（huàn）

[English, Wilhelm-Baynes]

  Huan / Dispersion [Dissolution]

[English, James Legge]
  
  LIX. The Hwân Hexagram

LINES:
(One moving line)

[Traditional Chinese]

  (Scripture)
  九五：渙汗其大號，渙王居，无咎。

  (Exegesis)
  王居无咎，正位也。

[Simplified Chinese]

  (Scripture)
  九五：涣汗其大号，涣王居，无咎。

  (Exegesis)
  王居无咎，正位也。

[English, Wilhelm-Baynes]

  (Scripture)
  Nine in the fifth place means:
  His loud cries are as dissolving as sweat.
  Dissolution! A king abides without blame.

  (Exegesis)
  Nine in the fifth place:
  a) His loud cries are as dissolving as sweat.
  Dissolution! A king abides without blame.
  b) “A king abides without blame.” He is in his proper place.

[English, James Legge]

  (Scripture)
  5. The fifth NINE, undivided, shows its subject amidst the dispersion issuing his great announcements as the perspiration (flows from his body). He scatters abroad (also) the accumulations in the royal granaries. There will be no error.

  (Exegesis)
  5. 'The accumulations of the royal (granaries) are dispersed, and there is no error:'--this is due to the correctness of the position.
